content.json:
# Azure Policy and Machine Configuration compliance (live)

Live view from Azure Resource Graph using **your** Azure identity and the selected scope. This workbook is read-only and reports Azure Policy / Machine Configuration results; it is **not** a CIS (or any other) certification or attestation.

Three different measures are always shown separately and never blended: **Azure Policy compliance %**, **check pass rate** and **coverage**. Stale, unknown-age, missing or no-data evidence is never shown as compliant.

All tabs except **History / Enhanced** are live and need nothing but Azure RBAC read access. The History tab is optional: it reads stored snapshots from a Log Analytics workspace that the standalone collector fills, and works only when that workspace is selected.

parameters.name: ResourceGroups
parameters.label: Resource groups
parameters.query:
resourcecontainers
| where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions/resourcegroups'
| distinct name
| project value = tolower(name), label = name
| order by label asc

parameters.name: Workspace
parameters.label: Log Analytics workspace (History tab, optional)
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces'
| project value = id, label = name
| order by label asc

parameters.name: CisDefinitionId
parameters.label: Native CIS policy definition GUID
parameters.description: Built-in policy definition GUID used only to label policy state rows as native CIS.

parameters.name: AzureBaselineDefinitionId
parameters.label: Azure Windows baseline policy definition GUID
parameters.description: Set to the GUID of the Azure Windows baseline policy definition in your estate; the placeholder labels no rows.

parameters.name: Category
parameters.label: Selected category
parameters.description: Set by selecting a category row.

parameters.name: CheckKey
parameters.label: Selected check
parameters.description: Set by selecting a check row.

parameters.name: MachineId
parameters.label: Selected machine
parameters.description: Set by selecting a machine row.

content.json:
### Metric definitions

| Measure | Numerator / denominator | Grain |
|---|---|---|
| Azure Policy compliance % | Compliant / (Compliant + NonCompliant); Exempt and other states are counted apart | policy state row (resource x assignment) |
| Check pass rate | unique checks Compliant / unique checks total, Fresh reports only | check (reasons are not checks) |
| Coverage | eligible machines with assignment / usable report / fresh report, over Windows-eligible machines | machine x family |
| Green machine | evidence Fresh (report endTime within 24h) AND reported state Compliant | machine x family |

A ratio with a zero denominator is shown as no data, never 0% or 100%.

content.query:
let policyRows = policyresources
    | where type =~ 'microsoft.policyinsights/policystates'
    | extend resourceId = tolower(tostring(properties.resourceId))
    | extend rg = tolower(coalesce(tostring(properties.resourceGroup), resourceGroup))
    | where '*' in ({ResourceGroups}) or rg in~ ({ResourceGroups})
    | extend defId = tolower(tostring(properties.policyDefinitionId))
    | extend family = case(
        defId endswith strcat('/', tolower('{CisDefinitionId}')), 'CISWindowsSecurityBaseline',
        defId endswith strcat('/', tolower('{AzureBaselineDefinitionId}')), 'AzureWindowsBaseline',
        'Other')
    | extend state = tostring(properties.complianceState)
    | project resourceId, assignmentId = tolower(tostring(properties.policyAssignmentId)), defId, family, state, stateTime = todatetime(properties.timestamp);
policyRows
| summarize compliant = countif(state == 'Compliant'), nonCompliant = countif(state == 'NonCompliant'), exempt = countif(state == 'Exempt'), other = countif(state !in ('Compliant', 'NonCompliant', 'Exempt')) by family
| extend denominator = compliant + nonCompliant
| extend percent = iff(denominator == 0, real(null), round(100.0 * compliant / denominator, 2))
| project family, percent, compliant, nonCompliant, denominator, exempt, other
| order by family asc
content.title: Azure Policy compliance % (resource x assignment states, per baseline family)
content.noDataMessage: No policy state rows in scope (no data is not compliance).

content.json:
**Query assumptions**
- Source: policyresources / microsoft.policyinsights/policystates (latest indexed state, not history).
- percent = compliant / (compliant + nonCompliant). Exempt and every other state are excluded from the denominator and shown as separate counts.
- Family is derived from the policy definition GUID parameters (CisDefinitionId, AzureBaselineDefinitionId); 'Other' is every other policy and is NOT a baseline family.
- This is NOT the check pass rate and NOT coverage. A machine with no policy state has no row here.

content.query:
let machines = resources
    | where type in~ ('microsoft.compute/virtualmachines', 'microsoft.hybridcompute/machines')
    | where '*' in ({ResourceGroups}) or resourceGroup in~ ({ResourceGroups})
    | extend machineId = tolower(id)
    | extend kind = iff(type =~ 'microsoft.hybridcompute/machines', 'ArcMachine', 'AzureVM')
    | extend osType = tolower(tostring(iff(kind == 'ArcMachine', properties.osType, properties.storageProfile.osDisk.osType)))
    | extend eligibility = case(osType == 'windows', 'Eligible', osType == 'linux', 'NotEligible', 'Unknown')
    | project machineId, machineName = name, kind, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, osType, eligibility;
let assignments = guestconfigurationresources
    | where type =~ 'microsoft.guestconfiguration/guestconfigurationassignments'
    | extend assignmentId = tolower(id)
    | extend machineId = tostring(split(assignmentId, '/providers/microsoft.guestconfiguration/')[0])
    | extend gcName = tostring(coalesce(properties.guestConfiguration.name, name))
    | extend family = case(gcName =~ 'AzureWindowsBaseline', 'AzureWindowsBaseline', gcName =~ 'CISWindowsSecurityBaseline', 'CISWindowsSecurityBaseline', 'Other')
    | where family != 'Other'
    | extend latest = properties.latestAssignmentReport
    | extend hasReport = isnotempty(tostring(latest))
    | extend reportEnd = todatetime(latest.endTime)
    | extend reportState = case(tolower(tostring(latest.complianceStatus)) == 'compliant', 'Compliant', tolower(tostring(latest.complianceStatus)) == 'noncompliant', 'NonCompliant', tolower(tostring(latest.complianceStatus)) == 'pending', 'Pending', 'Unknown')
    | extend rank = coalesce(reportEnd, datetime(1900-01-01))
    | project assignmentId, machineId, family, gcName, gcVersion = tostring(properties.guestConfiguration.version), hasReport, reportEnd, reportState, rank, resources = latest.resources;
let evidence = machines
    | mv-expand family = dynamic(['AzureWindowsBaseline', 'CISWindowsSecurityBaseline'])
    | extend family = tostring(family)
    | join kind=leftouter (assignments | summarize arg_max(rank, *) by machineId, family) on machineId, family
    | extend ageSeconds = datetime_diff('second', now(), reportEnd)
    | extend quality = case(
        eligibility == 'Unknown', 'UnknownApplicability',
        isempty(assignmentId), 'MissingAssignment',
        not(hasReport), 'NoReport',
        isnull(reportEnd), 'UnknownAge',
        ageSeconds <= 86400, 'Fresh',
        'Stale')
    | extend reportedState = iff(hasReport == true and quality != 'UnknownApplicability', reportState, '')
    | extend green = quality == 'Fresh' and reportedState == 'Compliant'
    | project machineId, machineName, kind, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, osType, eligibility, family, assignmentId, gcVersion, hasReport, reportEnd, ageSeconds, quality, reportedState, green, resources;
let freshChecks = evidence
    | where quality == 'Fresh'
    | mv-expand r = resources
    | extend checkKey = tostring(r.resourceId)
    | where isnotempty(checkKey)
    | extend status = iff(tolower(tostring(r.complianceStatus)) in ('true', 'compliant'), 'Compliant', 'NonCompliant')
    | extend reasonCount = coalesce(array_length(r.reasons), 0)
    | summarize checkStatus = iff(countif(status == 'NonCompliant') > 0, 'NonCompliant', 'Compliant'), reasonCount = sum(reasonCount) by machineId, machineName, family, checkKey
    | extend category = coalesce(extract(@'^\[([^\]]+)\]', 1, checkKey), 'Uncategorized');
let counts = freshChecks
    | summarize total = count(), passed = countif(checkStatus == 'Compliant') by family;
let excluded = evidence
    | summarize reportsExcludedAsNotFresh = countif(quality in ('Stale', 'UnknownAge')) by family;
excluded
| join kind=leftouter counts on family
| extend total = coalesce(total, 0), passed = coalesce(passed, 0)
| extend percent = iff(total == 0, real(null), round(100.0 * passed / total, 2))
| project family, percent, passed, failed = total - passed, total, reportsExcludedAsNotFresh
| order by family asc
content.title: Check pass rate (unique checks, latest Fresh report per machine and family)
content.noDataMessage: No Fresh report with checks in scope.

content.json:
**Query assumptions**
- Source: guestconfigurationresources assignments; checks are the unique properties.latestAssignmentReport.resources[].resourceId per report.
- percent = unique checks Compliant / unique checks total. Reasons are never counted as checks.
- Only reports with endTime within 24h of now() are included. Stale and unknown-age reports are excluded (reportsExcludedAsNotFresh) and are never treated as passing.
- A duplicate check key within one report keeps the worst status (matches the app normalizer).
- ARG exposes the latest report only; it is not a guarantee of full report content. Compare with the report GET for a selected machine.

content.json:

- One row per machine x baseline family. green requires quality == Fresh AND reportedState == Compliant; every other row shows the evidence-quality reason.
- machineId is the lower-cased full ARM ID, so duplicate machine names in different subscriptions or resource groups stay distinct.
- Arc vs Azure VM is decided by resource type, never by name or tag.

content.query:
let machines = resources
    | where type in~ ('microsoft.compute/virtualmachines', 'microsoft.hybridcompute/machines')
    | where '*' in ({ResourceGroups}) or resourceGroup in~ ({ResourceGroups})
    | extend machineId = tolower(id)
    | extend kind = iff(type =~ 'microsoft.hybridcompute/machines', 'ArcMachine', 'AzureVM')
    | extend osType = tolower(tostring(iff(kind == 'ArcMachine', properties.osType, properties.storageProfile.osDisk.osType)))
    | extend eligibility = case(osType == 'windows', 'Eligible', osType == 'linux', 'NotEligible', 'Unknown')
    | project machineId, machineName = name, kind, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, osType, eligibility;
let assignments = guestconfigurationresources
    | where type =~ 'microsoft.guestconfiguration/guestconfigurationassignments'
    | extend assignmentId = tolower(id)
    | extend machineId = tostring(split(assignmentId, '/providers/microsoft.guestconfiguration/')[0])
    | extend gcName = tostring(coalesce(properties.guestConfiguration.name, name))
    | extend family = case(gcName =~ 'AzureWindowsBaseline', 'AzureWindowsBaseline', gcName =~ 'CISWindowsSecurityBaseline', 'CISWindowsSecurityBaseline', 'Other')
    | where family != 'Other'
    | extend latest = properties.latestAssignmentReport
    | extend hasReport = isnotempty(tostring(latest))
    | extend reportEnd = todatetime(latest.endTime)
    | extend reportState = case(tolower(tostring(latest.complianceStatus)) == 'compliant', 'Compliant', tolower(tostring(latest.complianceStatus)) == 'noncompliant', 'NonCompliant', tolower(tostring(latest.complianceStatus)) == 'pending', 'Pending', 'Unknown')
    | extend rank = coalesce(reportEnd, datetime(1900-01-01))
    | project assignmentId, machineId, family, gcName, gcVersion = tostring(properties.guestConfiguration.version), hasReport, reportEnd, reportState, rank, resources = latest.resources;
let evidence = machines
    | mv-expand family = dynamic(['AzureWindowsBaseline', 'CISWindowsSecurityBaseline'])
    | extend family = tostring(family)
    | join kind=leftouter (assignments | summarize arg_max(rank, *) by machineId, family) on machineId, family
    | extend ageSeconds = datetime_diff('second', now(), reportEnd)
    | extend quality = case(
        eligibility == 'Unknown', 'UnknownApplicability',
        isempty(assignmentId), 'MissingAssignment',
        not(hasReport), 'NoReport',
        isnull(reportEnd), 'UnknownAge',
        ageSeconds <= 86400, 'Fresh',
        'Stale')
    | extend reportedState = iff(hasReport == true and quality != 'UnknownApplicability', reportState, '')
    | extend green = quality == 'Fresh' and reportedState == 'Compliant'
    | project machineId, machineName, kind, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, osType, eligibility, family, assignmentId, gcVersion, hasReport, reportEnd, ageSeconds, quality, reportedState, green, resources;
let freshChecks = evidence
    | where quality == 'Fresh'
    | mv-expand r = resources
    | extend checkKey = tostring(r.resourceId)
    | where isnotempty(checkKey)
    | extend status = iff(tolower(tostring(r.complianceStatus)) in ('true', 'compliant'), 'Compliant', 'NonCompliant')
    | extend reasonCount = coalesce(array_length(r.reasons), 0)
    | summarize checkStatus = iff(countif(status == 'NonCompliant') > 0, 'NonCompliant', 'Compliant'), reasonCount = sum(reasonCount) by machineId, machineName, family, checkKey
    | extend category = coalesce(extract(@'^\[([^\]]+)\]', 1, checkKey), 'Uncategorized');
freshChecks
| where machineId == tolower('{MachineId}')
| where '{Family}' == '*' or family == '{Family}'
| project family, category, checkKey, checkStatus, reasonCount
| order by checkStatus desc, category asc, checkKey asc

content.json:
**Query assumptions**
- Requires a machine row selected above. Shows the latest report only when it is Fresh; a Stale, unknown-age or missing report is explained by the evidence quality above, never rendered as passing.
- Checks are unique resourceId values; reasonCount is not a check count.

### Evidence and limitations

- **Live tabs only show the latest state.** Resource Graph holds the latest indexed state. There is no durable history, so no posture trend is shown on them. Stored snapshots need the enhanced mode (History tab, Log Analytics) or the standalone app.
- **Resource Graph is a projection.** It can lag, scrubs some data and is not guaranteed to expose every report property (completeness, expected/actual values, history). Verify against the Machine Configuration report for a selected machine.
- **Fresh** means the report endTime is within 24 hours of the time the query runs; older is Stale, a missing time is UnknownAge. Neither is ever treated as passing.
- **Reasons are not checks.** One check can carry several reasons; only unique check keys are counted.
- **Native CIS Windows Server is a preview offering with unverified applicability.** Missing CIS assignments are 'assessment unavailable', not failures and not compliance. AzureWindowsBaseline and CISWindowsSecurityBaseline are separate families; a cross-reference is not equivalence.
- **No certification claim.** Categories come from the check identifier prefix when present. No benchmark control mapping is asserted without verified provenance.
- **Scope and permissions.** Results contain only what your Azure RBAC allows; parameters filter the view but are not authorization. Row counts above Resource Graph limits (1,000 rows per page in the portal grid, expansion limits) can truncate results; narrow the scope if a grid reports truncation.

content.query:
policyresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.authorization/policyexemptions'
| extend rg = tolower(coalesce(tostring(properties.resourceGroup), resourceGroup))
| where '*' in ({ResourceGroups}) or rg in~ ({ResourceGroups}) or rg == ''
| extend expiresOn = todatetime(properties.expiresOn)
| extend expiresInDays = datetime_diff('day', expiresOn, now())
| project name, exemptionCategory = tostring(properties.exemptionCategory), policyAssignmentId = tostring(properties.policyAssignmentId), expiresOn, expiresInDays, subscriptionId
| order by expiresOn asc

content.json:
**Query assumptions**
- Source: policyresources / microsoft.authorization/policyexemptions. Availability of this type in ARG and the exact property names (expiresOn, exemptionCategory) are unverified; see docs/workbook.md.
- Expiry is shown in UTC; an empty expiresOn means no expiry was exposed.

### History / Enhanced mode (optional, Log Analytics)

This tab reads **stored snapshots** that the standalone collector delivered to a Log Analytics workspace. It is not live: every value is as of the collector snapshot time shown in the first table, and **delivery lag** (ingestion time minus snapshot time) shows how far behind the workspace is. Compare with the live tabs, which query Azure directly.

- Select the **Log Analytics workspace** and **Time range** in the parameters above. The subscription and resource-group filters do **not** scope this tab: log rows are filtered by workspace access, not by those parameters. Access to the workspace is not authorization for the underlying Azure resources; use resource-context access or one workspace per security boundary.
- History starts when the collector first delivered data and can have gaps (collector or delivery outages). Missing rows are shown as missing, never inferred.
- Interactive history covers up to 13 calendar months when the tables were deployed with the provided retention setting.
- Results describe Azure Policy / Machine Configuration reports; they are not a CIS certification.
**No Log Analytics workspace selected.** Choose one in the *Log Analytics workspace* parameter to see history. The History tab is optional; every other tab works without it.

content.query:
ComplianceCollectionRuns_CL
| extend IngestedAt = ingestion_time()
| summarize IngestedAt = min(IngestedAt), CollectionStatus = take_any(CollectionStatus), ReportsInserted = take_any(ReportsInserted), MachineCount = take_any(MachineCount), ErrorCount = take_any(ErrorCount) by RunId, SnapshotTime = TimeGenerated
| extend DeliveryLagMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', IngestedAt, SnapshotTime), SnapshotAgeHours = round(datetime_diff('minute', now(), SnapshotTime) / 60.0, 1)
| project SnapshotTime, RunId, CollectionStatus, MachineCount, ReportsInserted, ErrorCount, IngestedAt, DeliveryLagMinutes, SnapshotAgeHours
| order by SnapshotTime desc
content.title: Collection runs and delivery lag (Logs snapshot time, not live)
content.noDataMessage: No collection runs in Log Analytics for the selected time range.

content.json:
**Query assumptions**
- Every time shown here is the collector snapshot time stored in Log Analytics. It is not the live state in Azure; the Overview tab is the live view.
- Delivery lag = Log Analytics ingestion time minus snapshot time. Retried deliveries show as larger lag. A missing recent run means the collector did not run or its Logs delivery is backlogged; neither is shown as compliance.
- Rows are de-duplicated on RunId because the Logs Ingestion API is not idempotent and retries can duplicate rows. The earliest ingestion time is used.
- CollectionStatus is the PostgreSQL collection result. Delivery problems never change it.

content.query:
PolicyComplianceSnapshots_CL
| summarize CollectionStatus = take_any(CollectionStatus), PolicyCompliancePercent = take_any(PolicyCompliancePercent), CheckPassPercent = take_any(CheckPassPercent), ChecksTotal = take_any(ChecksTotal), ReportsExcludedAsNotFresh = take_any(ReportsExcludedAsNotFresh), EligibleMachines = take_any(EligibleMachines), FreshReportPercent = take_any(FreshReportPercent) by RunId, Family, SnapshotTime = TimeGenerated
| sort by Family asc, SnapshotTime asc
| extend CheckPassDelta = iff(Family == prev(Family) and isnotnull(CheckPassPercent) and isnotnull(prev(CheckPassPercent)), round(CheckPassPercent - prev(CheckPassPercent), 2), real(null))
| extend EligibleMachinesChange = iff(Family == prev(Family), EligibleMachines - prev(EligibleMachines), long(null))
| order by SnapshotTime desc, Family asc
content.title: Stored snapshots per baseline family (policy compliance %, check pass rate and coverage kept separate)
content.noDataMessage: No stored snapshots in Log Analytics for the selected time range.

content.json:
**Query assumptions**
- One row per collection run and family. The three measures are never blended; a null percentage means a zero denominator, not 0% or 100%.
- Deltas compare consecutive stored snapshots of the same family. Gaps between snapshots (outages, skipped runs) are not interpolated. EligibleMachinesChange shows a changing cohort; compare trends only when it is zero.
- Six-hour sampling is not continuous assessment. Partial or failed runs keep their CollectionStatus and are never hidden.

content.query:
let latestSnapshot = toscalar(ComplianceCollectionRuns_CL | summarize max(TimeGenerated));
let latestEnd = MachineConfigReports_CL
    | summarize ReportEndTime = max(ReportEndTime) by MachineId, Family;
let latestReport = MachineConfigReports_CL
    | join kind=inner latestEnd on MachineId, Family, ReportEndTime
    | summarize ReportId = min(ReportId) by MachineId, Family, ReportEndTime;
let dedupedChecks = MachineConfigChecks_CL
    | summarize CheckStatus = take_any(ComplianceStatus), CheckName = take_any(CheckName), CheckCategory = take_any(Category) by ReportId, CheckKey;
let logsFreshChecks = latestReport
    | where ReportEndTime >= latestSnapshot - 24h
    | join kind=inner dedupedChecks on ReportId
    | extend Category = iff(isempty(CheckCategory), 'Uncategorized', CheckCategory)
    | project MachineId, Family, ReportId, ReportEndTime, CheckKey, CheckName, CheckStatus, Category;
logsFreshChecks
| where '{Family}' == '*' or Family == '{Family}'
| summarize totalChecks = count(), failedChecks = countif(CheckStatus == 'NonCompliant'), distinctChecks = dcount(CheckKey), machinesAffected = dcountif(MachineId, CheckStatus == 'NonCompliant') by Family, Category
| extend failedPercent = iff(totalChecks == 0, real(null), round(100.0 * failedChecks / totalChecks, 2))
| order by failedChecks desc

content.json:
**Query assumptions**
- Uses the latest stored report per machine and family whose end time is within 24 hours of the latest stored collection snapshot. Older reports are excluded and not counted as passing.
- Only reports delivered to Log Analytics are visible. Reports stored by the app before the sink was enabled are absent, so a machine can look stale or missing here even though the app has data.
- Counts are unique (machine, check) pairs after de-duplicating retried deliveries on (ReportId, CheckKey). Category comes from the source check identifier prefix; no control mapping is claimed.

let latestEnd = MachineConfigReports_CL

let latestReport = MachineConfigReports_CL
    | join kind=inner latestEnd on MachineId, Family, ReportEndTime
    | summarize ReportId = min(ReportId) by MachineId, Family, ReportEndTime;

    | where ReportEndTime >= latestSnapshot - 24h

content.json:
**Query assumptions**
- Counts stored (machine, check) rows by the day the report ended. This describes the reports that were stored, not a fleet snapshot: a machine whose report did not change contributes no new rows.
- Use it to see where failures concentrate over time. Use the fleet-wide category summary for the current estate and the stored snapshots for the metric trend.

content.query:
MachineConfigReports_CL
| summarize ComplianceStatus = take_any(ComplianceStatus) by MachineId, Family, ReportEndTime, ReportId
| sort by MachineId asc, Family asc, ReportEndTime asc
| extend PreviousStatus = iff(MachineId == prev(MachineId) and Family == prev(Family), prev(ComplianceStatus), '')
| extend Change = case(PreviousStatus == 'Compliant' and ComplianceStatus == 'NonCompliant', 'Regression', PreviousStatus == 'NonCompliant' and ComplianceStatus == 'Compliant', 'Recovery', '')
| where Change != ''
| summarize Regressions = countif(Change == 'Regression'), Recoveries = countif(Change == 'Recovery'), LastChange = max(ReportEndTime) by MachineId, Family
| order by Regressions desc, LastChange desc
content.title: Drift: regressions and recoveries per machine and family
content.noDataMessage: No state changes between stored reports in the selected time range.

content.json:
**Query assumptions**
- Compares consecutive stored reports of the same machine and family: Compliant to NonCompliant is a regression, NonCompliant to Compliant is a recovery. Other state changes are ignored.
- Only reports delivered to Log Analytics within the selected time range are compared. A missing report (outage, retention) hides a change; it is never inferred.
- Machines are keyed by the lower-cased full ARM id, so duplicate names stay distinct.
